clue.text: River vessel by centre of loch with relative aboard

parts.note: a pot is a vessel for cooking or holding liquid

indicators.note: someone aboard is inside a vessel, so one piece goes inside another
the centre of a word is its middle, so only the inner letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of the four-letter word
Ma is mother, a relative

explanation.surface: A boat moored beside the middle of a Scottish lake, with a family member on board.
explanation.walkthrough: The relative goes inside the middle pair of letters of loch, and the vessel stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Potomac is the American river that flows past Washington DC.

clue.text: Yankee suckers Kensit and Cline caught?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: American slang for easily fooled people
second meaning: the English actress Kensit and the American country singer Cline share a first name; the plural names the pair

explanation.walkthrough: Patsy Kensit is an English actress and Patsy Cline was an American country singer; 'caught?' hints that dupes are people who get caught out.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang a patsy is a person easily taken advantage of, a dupe or sucker.

clue.text: Shelter close to hut with weapon

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

parts.note: the closing letter of hut
an épée is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: A refuge built near a hut, stocked with arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A tepee is a conical tent used by Plains peoples, a kind of shelter.

clue.text: Good tooth 60% twisted

indicators.note: twisted here means turned round, applied to only three fifths of the word, its tail end

parts.note: a molar is a back grinding tooth

explanation.surface: A decent tooth that has become partly crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Only three of the five letters, 60%, are turned round: the last three, leaving the first two in place.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a moral is a lesson in good conduct, and as an adjective moral means virtuous or good.

clue.text: Hood worn by bishop on the Spanish instrument

indicators.note: a garment worn by someone surrounds them, so the clothing wraps round what follows

parts.note: a cowl is a monk's hood
B is the chess notation for bishop
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A hooded garment worn by a bishop who is wearing it in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The hood is worn by, so wraps round, both the bishop and the Spanish article.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowbell is a bell hung on a cow and also used as a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Heading to port, some called at iconic fortress

indicators.note: port is a ship's left side, so in an across entry the letters run right to left
some means a portion of the words that follow, a run of their letters

parts.note: a run of letters straddling the three words

explanation.surface: A ship heading for harbour stopped at a famous fortress on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is the left side of a ship, so heading to port in an across clue means reading leftwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress, typically one commanding a city.

clue.text: Forecaster following Charlie's boat

indicators.note: coming after places one piece behind the other in the order of the entry

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an oracle foretells the future

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster's boat, coming after Charlie's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the forecaster after Charlie.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round Welsh boat made of wicker covered with hide.

clue.text: Boiler settler stripped at bottom of wood

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the end, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: teak is a hardwood

indicators.note: stripped means divested of its outer covering, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: settler without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A colonist, stripped of clothes, standing at the edge of a forest beside a boiler.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'at bottom of' places the trimmed settler below the wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A teakettle is a vessel for boiling water, so it is a boiler in a cryptic sense.

clue.text: Gadget from US state briefly in file on locker

indicators.note: said briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a doc is a document file
Ohio cut short by its last letter
a key locks things

explanation.surface: A device taken from an American state, filed in a document on a storage locker.
explanation.walkthrough: The shortened state sits inside the file, and in a down clue 'on' puts that above the locker.
explanation.definitionFit: A doohickey is an informal, chiefly American word for a small gadget whose name you forget.

clue.text: Northern bird below city light

indicators.note: in a down entry what is below comes later, so these pieces follow the other

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
N is the abbreviation for northern
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A northern seabird seen below a brightly lit city.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'below' puts the northern bird after the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp, a source of light.

clue.text: Spinner meets artist of the highest standing

parts.note: a top is a spinning toy
a drawer is one who draws

explanation.surface: A spin bowler encounters a painter of great renown.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinner in cricket is a slow bowler who spins the ball; here it is the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer is an idiom for the best quality or highest social class.

clue.text: Deck trouble confronting sailors

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Problems on a ship's deck with the crew facing up to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' is the verb, to decorate, not the floor of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something out is to decorate it, which is what adorn means.

clue.text: Pack of diamonds fellow regularly dropped by base

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

indicators.note: dropping at regular intervals means every other letter is lost and the rest kept

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of fellow
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A pack of cards of the diamond suit, with a man repeatedly dropping them on the base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' here is pack ice, the floating mass of frozen sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice floe is a sheet of floating ice, the stuff that makes up pack ice.

clue.text: Vicar in charge blocks up church opening

indicators.note: something that blocks up an opening sits inside it, plugging the gap

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Rev is the title of a vicar, the Reverend
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A vicar, being in charge, has a hole in his church boarded up.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevice is a narrow crack or opening in a rock or wall.

clue.text: Guru peels off sticker

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters are out of order and need rearranging

parts.note: the fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: A spiritual teacher peels away a label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' means bad or not right, so the letters go wrong and must be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Superglue is a very strong adhesive, something that makes things stick.

clue.text: ID numbers attached to rubbish suit?

parts.note: PINs are personal identification numbers
tripe is nonsense

explanation.surface: A judgement that security codes are linked to a load of junk.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example: a pinstripe is a suit of a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinstripe is a suit with fine stripes, the uniform of bankers and businessmen.

clue.text: Criminal pair sends speed

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked or bent, so these letters are bent into another order

parts.note: the fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: A crooked duo dispatches drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed' is also slang for an amphetamine, which fits the criminal surface but is the quickness meaning here.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapidness is the quality of being quick, which is speed.

clue.text: Distinctive feature of Barbie's letter opener?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sign or mark that characterises something
second meaning, read as two words: how Barbie would start a note to her doll boyfriend

explanation.walkthrough: A letter opener sounds like a paper knife, but here it is the greeting at the head of a letter: Barbie writing to Ken.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is a symbol or sign, a characteristic mark that stands for something.

clue.text: Reds with power adopt a responsible attitude

parts.note: Man U, Manchester United football club, are nicknamed the Red Devils or Reds
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: Communists with political clout decide to behave sensibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reds' suggests communists; here it is the nickname of Manchester United, the English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To man up is an idiom for taking responsibility and facing a difficulty bravely.

clue.text: Blokes arrested by London police with old trophy

indicators.note: people arrested by police are held in custody, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
blokes are men
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Some lads arrested by the Metropolitan Police were carrying an old cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake, and a trophy is a souvenir kept as a reminder of a success.

clue.text: Love Handles autobiography by bore delivered

parts.note: Spare is the title of Prince Harry's 2023 memoir

indicators.note: a speech is delivered out loud, so the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: to bore someone is to tire them

explanation.surface: Someone named Love handles the delivery of a memoir by a tedious author.
explanation.walkthrough: Delivered means spoken, so the word for bore is heard and spelt the British way as the wheel's rubber.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare tyre is jokey slang for a roll of fat round the waist, the same thing as love handles.

clue.text: Condition of sheep that is at bottom of ditch

parts.note: to ditch something is to scrap it
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A sickly sheep is found lying at the bottom of a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'at bottom of' puts that is below the ditch; ditch is a verb, not a trench.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapie is a fatal brain disease of sheep and goats, a prion illness.

clue.text: Worker with helper bottling cold medicine

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

indicators.note: bottling means enclosing something in a container, so one piece holds another

parts.note: an aid is a helper or assistant
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: An employee and an assistant hold in a cold remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: An antacid is a medicine that neutralises stomach acid to relieve indigestion.

clue.text: Poem from record carried by electronic signal

parts.note: e- is short for electronic, as in email

indicators.note: a load carried by something is held within it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a cue is a signal to act
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A poem recovered from a recording transmitted electronically.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclogue is a short pastoral poem, often a dialogue between shepherds, as in Virgil.

clue.text: A lot of Antipodean guards bit fighter

indicators.note: guards stand around what they protect, so one piece encloses the other
a lot of means most but not all, so the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a Maori is a native New Zealander, from the Antipodes
a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: Many Australasian security guards bit a boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Antipodean loses its last letter, then holds the bit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who kills the bull.

clue.text: Fun playing with lute in musical

indicators.note: playing suggests fooling about, so the letters are jumbled into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Having fun strumming a lute in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musical' looks like the noun, a stage show, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuneful means melodious, full of pleasant tunes, which is musical in the adjective sense.

clue.text: New song about a South African native

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: about as in turned about, so the word faces the other way

parts.note: a lay is a ballad or song
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh tune about one person born in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope native to southern Africa.

clue.text: Blond given last of fizzy Sprite

parts.note: fair hair is blond

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the final letter of fizzy

explanation.surface: A fair-haired person handed the end of a fizzy Sprite drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Sprite is a lemonade brand, which suits fizzy, but here it means a spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is an elf or small supernatural being, a synonym for a fairy.

clue.text: Sound hooter across Italy

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so one piece stretches round the other

parts.note: hooter is slang for nose
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A car horn blares across Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: A hooter suggests a horn, but here it is the slang for a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is any sound, especially a loud or unwanted one.

clue.text: Outward appearance of group getting on

parts.note: a pack is a group of animals or people
getting on means growing old

explanation.surface: The look of a band whose members are growing old.
explanation.definitionFit: Packaging can mean the way something is presented to the public, its image or outward appearance.

clue.text: Manage poetry poet barely comprehends

indicators.note: comprehends in its old sense of includes or takes in, so one piece holds another
barely read as made bare, stripped of its outer letters, leaving the middle

parts.note: poet stripped bare of its outer letters
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A poet can barely understand how to deal with poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' means stripped bare, its outside layer removed, not 'scarcely'.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise or be in charge, which is to manage.

clue.text: Runner obstructed by Mary cycling … oh no!

indicators.note: something obstructed has a blockage in its middle, so another piece sits inside it
going round in a cycle moves the front letter round to the back of the name

parts.note: the Dee is a river, and a river runs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner is blocked by Mary on her bike, and cries in dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: Cycling moves the first letter of the name to the end. A runner is crossword shorthand for a river; the Dee flows in Scotland and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Deary me is an exclamation of dismay or sorrow, much like saying oh no.
